answers.answer: In 3 players, tied leaders gain no coin and the unique last player pays 1 coin. In an unequal 2-player Census, the unique leader gains 1 coin, while the last player never pays.
answers.evidence: “unique leader gains 1 coin; a tied lead gives no coin”; “In a 2-player game the last player never pays” (Turn Structure—Census).

answers.answer: No. Draw at most two because free Market spaces limit draws, even though allowance is six. Unused Followers already on the Market remain there between rounds and occupy capacity.
answers.evidence: “Draw any number up to the allowance … limited by free Market spaces”; “Unused Market Followers remain between rounds and occupy capacity.”

answers.answer: You may fill an action over multiple rounds, but cannot execute it until all required spaces are occupied by Followers or legal Technology (except Town Hall, where one space suffices). You may save a fully activated action for a later round. When an ordinary action is executed, its Followers return to your bag; Technology remains on its space.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure—Planning and Actions: “fill an action gradually over multiple rounds”; “An activation can be saved”; after ordinary action, Followers return to bag and Technology stays.

answers.answer: Starting with Start Player, players go clockwise repeatedly and take one activated action or pass per turn. Passing ends your participation for the Action Phase; you cannot return later. Any unused activation keeps its Followers on the board for future rounds.
answers.evidence: “taking one activated action or passing per turn”; “Passing ends your participation”; unused activations “keep their Followers on the board for future rounds.”

answers.answer: Farm House recruits a Farmer into your bag, advances your Farmers Track one space, and gives the good depicted at that space.
answers.evidence: Actions table: “Put a new Farmer in your bag; advance Farmers Track one space and take its depicted good.”

answers.answer: Village chooses one neutral recruit, which goes into your bag, and advances that profession’s track one space: Boatman gains depicted coins (or a Citizen instead at the last space if first there); Craftsman gains a Technology tile; Trader gains a Place Tile.
answers.evidence: Village recruitment bullets specify the recruit goes in your bag, track advancement, and rewards for Boatman, Craftsman, and Trader.

answers.answer: No. The newly gained Technology is used only after you pass, so it cannot help another action that round after that pass. Your first Technology must replace a Farmer; later Technology can replace any profession except Monk. At most one Technology may be at a Place, never at a Place requiring only one Follower, and it cannot be moved once placed.
answers.evidence: “use it only after you pass”; Technology rules: first replaces Farmer, later any except Monk, at most one per Place, not at a one-Follower Place, cannot be moved.

answers.answer: No. The first Trader-track advance permits category I only; every later advance permits category I or II. Players may inspect the stacks at any time.
answers.evidence: Trader recruitment and Setup: “first Traders Track advance permits category I only; every later advance allows I or II”; “Players may inspect these stacks at any time.”

answers.answer: University recruits a Scholar into your bag, advances the Scholars Track, and gives its depicted Development Points. Castle recruits a Knight into your bag and advances the Knights Track; the fourth Knight leaves the allowance at 7, with no increase at that step, and the first player to reach that space gets its Citizen. Monastery recruits a Monk into your bag with no extra track reward. Once a character track is at its last space, you cannot take that corresponding action again.
answers.evidence: Actions table, Castle rewards, and Character-track limits.

answers.answer: A Monk may replace any profession on ordinary actions. A Knight or Technology cannot replace a required Monk. Monks and other substitutions cannot replace the exact professions depicted on Beneficial Deeds.
answers.evidence: Monks: “a Monk can replace any other profession. The reverse is forbidden”; Deeds require “exact professions.”

answers.answer: One Ship or Wagon action moves your Merchant along one connection to one adjacent town (Ship uses a Waterway; Wagon a Road). You may take at most one good from that connection, choosing one if two lie there. An empty connection is legal and yields no good.
answers.evidence: Movement and goods: one adjacent town along one connection, “one” good and choose one if several; empty connections legal.

answers.answer: Guildhall builds one Trading Station in the town where your Merchant is. A town with any player’s station cannot receive another, except Orléans, where each player may build one station.
answers.evidence: Building: Guildhall requires Merchant in the town; occupied towns barred; “Orléans is the exception: each player may build one station there.”

answers.answer: Scriptorium gives 1 Development Point (move one space on the Development Track). Moving onto or past a coin space gives its depicted coins; the first player onto or past a Citizen space collects that Citizen; reaching or passing a Development Status space immediately changes Status to its shown value.
answers.evidence: Actions table for Scriptorium; Scoring: moving “onto or past” coin/Citizen spaces and reaching/passing Status spaces.

answers.answer: Town Hall activates with one or two eligible neutral Followers and can send one or both in one action; marked starting Followers cannot be used. Each goes permanently to a free Beneficial Deed space matching its exact profession, possibly on different Deeds, and earns the depicted 1, 2, or 3 coins; Canalization gives a choice of 1 coin or 1 Development Point. Filling the last space on a Deed earns its Citizen.
answers.evidence: Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds: one or two neutral Followers; exact matching free spaces; rewards; Canalization choice; last space earns Citizen; starting Followers barred.

answers.answer: Pilgrimage prohibits Monk recruitment during the Action Phase; it applies before the Event Phase. Other events are resolved for all players in Phase 6. Round 1 always opens with Pilgrimage.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: Pilgrimage affects Phase 5; events otherwise wait until Phase 6. Setup puts the lighter Pilgrimage tile on top of the Hour Glass stack.

answers.answer: Wool and wine: wine is food, but wool is not; grain, cheese, or wine may be paid, and paid food goes to the Goods Market. If you cannot pay food, you owe 5 coins; if you cannot pay those coins, you undergo torture for the shortfall.
answers.evidence: Harvest: pay one grain, cheese, or wine to Goods Market; otherwise 5 coins; wool and brocade are not food; inability to pay leads to torture.

answers.answer: For a neutral Scholar, return it to its game-board supply, where it is recruitable again; do not move its track marker back. For your marked starting Trader, keep it and lose no Follower; do not redraw.
answers.evidence: Plague event states neutral returns to supply and track does not move back; marked starting Follower is kept, no loss, no redraw.

answers.answer: Pay the one available coin, then cover each of the two missing coins with one eligible item (any mix): a built or unbuilt station, a random eligible Follower drawn only from your bag, a Development Point moved left (not onto or past a coin space), a Goods Tile, Place Tile, or Technology tile. Followers on Market or Action Spaces are ineligible; marked starters are returned and redrawn until an eligible neutral is drawn. Surrendered items are removed from the game.
answers.evidence: Torture rules: each missing coin replaced by listed item; restrictions on bag-only draw and Development movement; surrendered items removed.

answers.answer: You cannot execute an action that provides an unavailable Character, Technology, or Goods tile, even if another part would still reward you. The action becomes available again as soon as the required tile is available, subject to its normal requirements. If the common coin supply is insufficient, players cannot receive coins at that moment.
answers.evidence: Limited supplies paragraph.

answers.answer: A tie for most built stations awards the bonus Citizen to nobody. Goods score grain/cheese/wine/wool/brocade at 1/2/3/4/5 points each. Stations and collected Citizens score (built stations + Citizens) × final Development Status. Highest total wins; a tie goes to the player furthest ahead on the Development Track, and if still tied they share victory.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions table and text; unique-most station rule says tie gives nobody the bonus Citizen.

answers.answer: Each player gets a board, bag, Merchant, 10 Trading Stations, 5 coins, 7 markers, and four marked starting Followers. Put starting Followers on the Market, Merchant in Orléans, and one marker on the first space of each six Character Tracks and the Development Track. Keep coins and unbuilt stations in front of you. The youngest player takes the Start Player token.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 2 and closing sentence.

answers.answer: Place both boards; sort neutral Followers into their game-board buildings, Technology into its supply, and coins nearby. Put 13 Citizens on marked board/Deed spaces and set the remaining Citizen aside for the final station award. Separate Place Tiles into categories I and II. In a four-player game, deal a shuffled good face up to every eligible Road/Waterway goods space; sort remaining goods face up in the Goods Market.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1, 3, and 5: 13 Citizens plus remaining set aside, sorted supplies and Place Tiles, all goods spaces filled in 4-player games.

answers.answer: For 3 players remove 2 neutral Farmers, Boatmen, Craftsmen, and Traders of each profession; remove 3 neutral Knights, Scholars, and Monks of each; remove 6 random goods; leave spaces marked 4 empty. For 2 players remove 4 of each neutral Farmer/Boatman/Craftsman/Trader; remove 6 of each neutral Knight/Scholar/Monk; remove 12 random goods; leave spaces marked 3 or 4 empty. Remove all starting Followers of unused colors.
answers.evidence: Fewer players table and text immediately above it.

answers.answer: Farm House: Boatman + Craftsman. Village: Farmer + Boatman + Craftsman. University: Farmer + Craftsman + Trader. Castle: Farmer + Boatman + Trader. Monastery: Scholar + Trader.
answers.evidence: Actions table, columns Place and Required Followers.

answers.answer: Ship: Farmer + Boatman + Knight. Wagon: Farmer + Trader + Knight. Guildhall: Farmer + Craftsman + Knight.
answers.evidence: Actions table, columns Place and Required Followers.

answers.answer: Scriptorium requires Knight + Scholar. Town Hall takes 1 or 2 eligible Followers; its detailed rule specifies neutral Followers, excluding your four marked starting Followers.
answers.evidence: Actions table and Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds paragraph.

answers.answer: Yes. You may decline two draws and for each declined draw move one Follower from an Action Space back to your Market. You may not move a Follower directly from one Action Space to another.
answers.evidence: Followers phase: for each declined draw, may move one Follower from an Action Space to Market; direct Action Space-to-Action Space movement is forbidden.

answers.answer: Yes. You may inspect your bag at any time, but must shuffle its contents afterward.
answers.evidence: Followers phase: “You may inspect your bag at any time, but shuffle its contents afterward.”

answers.answer: The seven phases are Hour Glass, Census, Followers, Planning, Actions, Event, Start Player. Pass the Start Player token left. Planning begins simultaneously; if order matters, proceed clockwise from Start Player. Event payments and necessary order-sensitive resolution proceed clockwise from Start Player. Coins paid go to the common supply; received coins come from it.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure lists phases and specifies clockwise planning/payment order and coin destinations.

answers.answer: Finish the entire 18th round, including its Event phase; scoring follows the round.
answers.evidence: “Finish the entire round in which the 18th Hour Glass tile is drawn, including its event. Before scoring…”

answers.answer: The uniquely ahead player on the Farmers Track gains the Census coin, regardless of how many Farmer tiles are in players’ bags.
answers.evidence: Census compares Farmers Track markers “regardless of how many Farmer tiles are currently in bags”; unique leader gains 1 coin.

answers.answer: Income pays coins equal to your current Development Status.
answers.evidence: Events table: “Income — Gain coins equal to Development Status.” Scoring text says Status is current and determines Income.

answers.answer: Eight goods means two complete groups of three, so pay 2 coins; goods types do not change the count. A shortfall causes torture.
answers.evidence: Taxes: count all goods, pay 1 coin per complete group of 3 (round down); shortfall causes torture.

answers.answer: You receive 4 coins, one per built Trading Station. Unbuilt reserve stations do not count.
answers.evidence: Trading Day pays 1 coin per built station; only built stations count for income.

answers.answer: Hayrick: Farmer; takes grain from Goods Market. Cheese Factory: Farmer + Farmer; takes cheese from Goods Market. Winery: Farmer + Trader; takes wine from Goods Market. Wool Manufacturer: Boatman + Trader; takes wool from Goods Market. Tailor Shop: Scholar + Trader; takes brocade from Goods Market. Each is unusable if that particular good is absent from the Goods Market.
answers.evidence: Base Place Tile table lists costs and goods from Goods Market; following sentence says a goods-producing Place cannot be used when its particular good is absent.

answers.answer: Shipping Line: Boatman, gain 1 Development Point. Brewery: Monk, gain 2 coins. Windmill: Craftsman + Craftsman, gain 2 coins and 1 Development Point. Library: Knight + Scholar, gain 2 Development Points.
answers.evidence: Base Place Tile table.

answers.answer: Any one Follower activates Pharmacy. Pay 1–3 coins; at two coins it advances two Development spaces. Zero or four coins are not allowed.
answers.evidence: Pharmacy table entry: “Any 1 Follower”; pay 1–3; one Development space per coin; minimum 1 and maximum 3.

answers.answer: Cellar: Monk + Scholar, 4 coins. Office: Scholar + Scholar, 1 coin per built Trading Station. Hospital: Boatman + Scholar, coins equal to current Development Status.
answers.evidence: Base Place Tile table; its Office and Hospital entries specify payout quantities.

answers.answer: Horse Wagon activates with Trader + Knight. It moves along one Road to an adjacent town and collects one good if available.
answers.evidence: Horse Wagon table entry.

answers.answer: Laboratory requires Scholar + Craftsman and gives a Technology tile, subject to the usual placement rules. Your first Technology cannot go there because it must replace a Farmer. A later Technology may go on either Laboratory space if none is already there and the usual constraints are met.
answers.evidence: Laboratory entry in base Place table.

answers.answer: Bathhouse requires a Farmer. Draw three Followers from your bag, choose two, and immediately put them on appropriate Action Spaces; none may go on Bathhouse. Return the third drawn Follower and the activating Bathhouse Follower to your bag.
answers.evidence: Bathhouse table entry.

answers.answer: Place the one tile that can legally go on an allowed Action Space. Return the other two drawn tiles and the activating Bathhouse Follower to your bag. If none can be placed, return all three drawn Followers and the activating Follower to your bag.
answers.evidence: Bathhouse entry: choose two but “If you can legally place only one or none, do so and return all other drawn Followers to the bag”; none may go on Bathhouse.

answers.answer: The summary says Bathhouse can place drawn Followers immediately on appropriate Action Spaces, and says actions may be chosen freely, but it does not specify whether an action completed during the Action Phase can be executed later in that same phase. That timing point is unsupported by the summary.
answers.evidence: Bathhouse: “immediately place them on appropriate Action Spaces”; Actions: “Choose your actions’ order freely.” No sentence states whether a newly completed action can be used later that phase.

answers.answer: Sacristy requires a Monk. If activated, it protects you from a negative event such as Harvest, Taxes, or Plague; during Phase 6, return its Monk to your bag instead of suffering the event.
answers.evidence: Sacristy table entry says activated protection against negative event examples and resolves during Phase 6.

answers.answer: No. Pilgrimage prohibits Monk recruitment during the Action Phase (Phase 5). Sacristy protection is used during Phase 6, so it does not override the earlier recruitment restriction.
answers.evidence: Pilgrimage: “No Monk recruitment in this round’s Action Phase”; Sacristy protection happens during Phase 6.

answers.answer: Herb Garden lets Boatmen replace Craftsmen, Traders, and Farmers on ordinary actions. It does not permit replacing Knights, Scholars, or Monks.
answers.evidence: Herb Garden table entry enumerates only Craftsmen, Traders, Farmers.

answers.answer: School lets Scholars replace other professions except Monks on ordinary actions. It has no activation cost or activation requirement. A Scholar cannot replace a required Monk.
answers.evidence: School: “No activation”; Scholars may replace other professions except Monks.

answers.answer: No. Beneficial Deeds require exact depicted professions, so Herb Garden or School substitutions cannot fill a differently depicted Deed space. Gunpowder Tower does not change the exact-type requirement.
answers.evidence: Town Hall paragraph says substitutions, including Place abilities, cannot replace exact Deed professions; Gunpowder rules say Deed spaces still require exact types.

answers.answer: Gunpowder Tower adds two Market spaces. During Phase 3 place one or two drawn Followers there. In Planning, move one or both to Action Spaces; alternatively, during Actions send one or both directly to Beneficial Deeds in a single action. Marked starting Followers cannot be sent, and Deeds still require exact professions.
answers.evidence: Gunpowder Tower table entry.

answers.answer: The unique leader gains 1 coin. The two tied players at the back pay nothing because tied last place pays nothing.
answers.evidence: Census: unique leader gains 1; tied last place pays nothing.

answers.answer: The unique player with the most built Trading Stations receives the set-aside Citizen after completing round 18, before scoring. That Citizen counts among collected Citizens in the station/Citizen scoring formula.
answers.evidence: Scoring text: finish round 18 including event; before scoring unique-most stations takes Citizen. Formula counts collected Citizens.

answers.answer: Remove the lighter Pilgrimage tile, shuffle the other 17 Hour Glass tiles face down, then put the lighter Pilgrimage on top. In Phase 1, Start Player reveals the top tile.
answers.evidence: Setup Hour Glass step and Turn Structure Phase 1.

answers.answer: Each remaining coin scores 1 victory point.
answers.evidence: Scoring table: Coins — 1 each.

answers.answer: Development Status starts at 1; initial Knight-track draw allowance is 4.
answers.evidence: Setup: “Development Status starts at 1; initial draw allowance is 4.”

answers.answer: Only lost Development Points can be regained. Surrendered goods, Followers, stations, Places, and Technology are removed from the game rather than returned to supplies.
answers.evidence: Torture: surrendered items are removed from game; “Only lost Development Points can be regained.”

answers.answer: You may choose your activated actions’ execution order freely.
answers.evidence: Actions phase: “Choose your actions’ order freely.”

answers.answer: It is available immediately, including during the current Action Phase.
answers.evidence: Trader recruitment: acquired Place and passive special ability “available immediately, including during the current Action Phase.”

answers.answer: You may send just one; Town Hall can send one or both.
answers.evidence: Town Hall: “In one Town Hall action, send one or both…”

answers.answer: The wording says you may take one good from the connection; it does not explicitly state whether taking is optional. Therefore whether you may leave an available good behind is unsupported by the summary.
answers.evidence: Movement and goods says “You may take one good from that connection” and “Empty Roads/Waterways are legal and yield no good,” but does not expressly address declining an available good.

answers.answer: You may send the second Follower on a later action turn in the same Action Phase, before passing; the transfers need not happen in one action.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: “You may send its two Followers in separate action turns during the same Action Phase, before you pass.”
